Read more about the Summer of Sovereignty and all related changes in the following blogs:

  • New Details on July Sovereignty Release Schedule
  • Sovereignty Transition and Deployment

I'm planning to start making my own wine in the next few weeks, but the one thing I'm nervous about is brewing 5 gallons of a wine only to discover I don't like that kind. In fact, this is the only reason I've not already started. The wine I've liked in the past has been fairly cheap and not listed which types of grape they used. I would just buy a few different bottles until I found one I liked.

Right now I'm going to the SAQ (the government liquor seller here in Quebec) and buying mini bottles of wines that list grape types. Is there a better way to go about this?

I've only made grape wine twice, the second time tasted better than the first but neither had a flavor that I would be happy with if I had bought them from a real winery or liquor store.
Also, a lot of the time when your cheap wine doesn't have a listed grape variety on it it's because it's a mix of different varieties. They do this to because some years the grapes or wine batches don't have the desired flavors so they rescue them by mixing them with others to make a more palatable wine. Having said that sometimes these cheap wines can taste really good.

Buy mini bottles if you like but most wineries will let you taste a variety of wines for free if you go there.

I hope you have fun and your wine turns out good. Can you let us know how it goes?

I did see that most wines in the stores around here have no grapes listed, and I expected it was for the reasons you state... it's a mix of whatever is cheap and will make the flavour they want. It also looks like some are mixed with juices, from what I've read on labels.

Last week I started getting some mini bottles from the SAQ (liquor store in Quebec) and I think I'll try making a Cabernet Sauvignon. I'm a little worried that my garage is going to be too warm right now, and I've heard doing it in your basement can leave you with hard to get rid of yeast smells.... so I might wait a month or two. Eventually I plan to get an old fridge or chest freezer to use as a fermenting chamber where I can control the temperature, but I have a few too many things to buy right now!

I'll try to remember to come back and leave an update.
